name: Baikal-GVD — southern Lake Baikal site
notes: The array is described as growing annually (12 clusters implied by 96 strings / 8 strings-per-cluster as of the winter 2023 season cited here; web search indicates further growth to 14-15 clusters by 2024-2025, but that could not be independently fetched and quoted this session, so only the 2023 status paper's own directly-quoted numbers are used in the data records). Only one representative cluster's footprint is drawn (geometry:baikal-gvd-cluster-footprint); the full multi-cluster array footprint is not stated by any source fetched this session and is not derived here (drawing a hexagonal-packing guess for 12+ clusters at 300 m spacing would assume a specific packing shape that is not itself sourced).

The onshore 'shore station' housing the control/DAQ systems is mentioned in secondary sources (~4 km from the lake site, near the Ivanovka river outfall) but no source fetched this session gives it a citable building-level position, and Overpass access was unreachable for most of this session (see map:amundsen-scott-south-pole-station's notes) so no OSM search for it could be completed. Left as a backlog item rather than drawn or guessed.

summary.plain: The southern basin of Lake Baikal, Siberia, where the growing Baikal-GVD neutrino telescope hangs its strings of light sensors about 3.6 km offshore and 1366 m down.
summary.technical: Local map for facility:baikal-deep-underwater-neutrino-telescope. One surveyed point (the collaboration's own published 51 46'N 104 24'E) and one derived ~120 m-diameter circle for a single cluster's string layout (per the 2023 status paper, arXiv:2309.16310); the full multi-cluster array footprint is not sourced and not drawn.
